prompt: One square detailed painterly naturalistic encyclopedia illustration of Japanese ryū, the water and rain dragon, in the conventional East Asian serpentine form seen in Japanese dragon paintings. One enormous long scaled winding snake-like body with a dragon head, long whiskers, small branched head horns, and four short clawed limbs, THREE claw toes on each visible foot; NO WINGS. Body coils gracefully through layered rain clouds above dark Japanese mountain water and a distant shrine. Full dragon from head to tail comfortably inside square frame, clear unbroken body silhouette and coherent limb attachments. Mood: powerful sacred water guardian, commanding majestic natural storm presence, awe and reverence, not malicious and not cute. Slate jade scales, muted silver whiskers, atmospheric painted rain and water, luminous storm light. Keep dragon associated with clouds, rainfall and water, no fire, no western bat wings, no extra heads, limbs or weapons, no people, no text or watermark. Single standalone scene, no panels.

Conventional Japanese three-claw form, whiskers and horns
